title: HarrowPoint onboarding orientation and compliance sync
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-02-25
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto transcript
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Jordan Lee (Redwood) — Marta Ruiz, Devon Price, Sana Ahmed, Tom Alvarez (HarrowPoint)
summary: Kickoff/orientation for onboarding HarrowPoint onto Redwood Inference. Covered current infra footprint, security/compliance requirements (SaaS vs VPC vs on-prem), pilot success criteria, and an initial runbook for a 4-week pilot. Agreed to provide security pack, pilot pricing, and a lightweight benchmark plan. Action items captured for both teams.
topics: Deployment model options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
Next steps, docs to share, and scheduling follow-ups
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll give a quick agenda and then jump in.
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: Yep thanks Alex, excited to get this started. Quick intro from our side, I'm Tom, CTO.
[00:18] Marta Ruiz: Marta here, lead of MLOps, we'll be owning the pilot day to day.
[00:23] Devon Price: Devon, platform eng, I'll handle infra bits.
[00:26] Sana Ahmed: Sana, security. I'll drive compliance questions.
[00:30] Alex Chen: Great thanks—Priya from our infra team will cover performance and Jordan on onboarding playbook. Priya over to you for a quick overview of the runtime.
[00:40] Priya Nair: Yeah hi all, so Redwood's runtime is built for continuous batching and KV cache management. We support hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC deployments. For pilots we usually recommend starting hosted to move fast unless you have hard data residency or air gap needs.
[01:05] Devon Price: Quick clarifying q: when you say hosted, is data persisted in any way? We need to know retention and where logs live.
[01:12] Jordan Lee: Good question. By default hosted requests are encrypted in transit and at rest, logs retained per our retention policy, we can configure retention windows and purge. We'll send the detailed security pack.
[01:26] Sana Ahmed: We need SOC 2 evidence and SAML SSO, also KMS integration for key control. Any HSM options?
[01:33] Priya Nair: We integrate with customer KMS; HSM-backed keys are supported in private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and you can bring keys via supported KMS providers. We'll attach our compliance deck and KMS integration guide.
[01:47] Marta Ruiz: From a success criteria perspective the pilot needs: 99th p95 latency under 350ms for our 512 token profile, cost per 1M tokens below our threshold, and zero-PHI leakage.
[02:00] Alex Chen: OK noted. On the latency side Priya, is 350ms plausible on hosted?
[02:05] Priya Nair: It depends on model and sequence length; for 512 tokens with Redwood-optimized models we can be sub-300ms for single-request latencies in most regions. But you'll see variance in cold starts; we can recommend warmup patterns and autoscaling configuration.
[02:22] Devon Price: If we run the pilot in a VPC, will we still get the same latency? Networking overhead adds jitter.
[02:29] Priya Nair: VPC adds a bit of egress/ingress latency; in practice it's 20–50ms depending on peering. We can run the benchmark with your VPC in a pilot.
[02:40] Tom Alvarez: Cost: what levers do we have—quantization, batching, or model selection?
[02:47] Priya Nair: All of the above. Redwood Optimize will give recommendations — quantized float16 or int8 variants, batching knobs, and cached prefixes for repeated prompts. We'll share an initial config tuned for latency/sla/cost tradeoff.
[03:02] Alex Chen: Let's talk timeline — 4-week pilot, week 0 discovery, week 1 integration and smoke tests, week 2 benchmark run, week 3 evaluation and wrap. Does that map to your expectations?
[03:14] Marta Ruiz: Yes that maps. We'll need an internal stakeholder list and the SSO work to be completed during week 1.
[03:21] Jordan Lee: On SSO, we support SAML and OIDC. Jordan: we'll need a test IdP and a list of accounts.
[03:30] Sana Ahmed: We'll provide a test IdP but we have to run a security scoping questionnaire first.
[03:36] Alex Chen: I'll drop the security questionnaire and our SOC2 report after the call.
[03:40] Devon Price: For the integration, what's the simplest approach for us to start—server-to-server API keys or VPC peering?
[03:47] Priya Nair: If you want rapid start, server-to-server API keys on hosted is fastest. If you require network isolation, VPC is the route — a private deployment or VPC-enabled private endpoints.
[03:58] Tom Alvarez: Our compliance team is sensitive to keys in hosted. We might need dedicated capacity or private.
[04:04] Alex Chen: Understood — we'll include a comparison doc.
[04:08] [04:08] Marta Ruiz: Are there specific data path diagrams to show where PII might touch? That's something our privacy folks want.
[04:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include a data flow diagram showing masking, routing, and optional on-prem connectors.
[04:20] Alex Chen: Quick note on benchmarks: Priya, propose a benchmark plan we can run—load drivers, sample prompts, and measurement windows.
[04:27] Priya Nair: We'll propose a 3-stage benchmark: single-request latencies, steady-state throughput at expected QPS, and failover/resilience scenarios. We'll include a spreadsheet for you to populate with your prompt sets.
[04:40] Devon Price: For tooling, do you expose tracing or per-token cost metrics?
[04:45] Jordan Lee: Yes, in Console you'll see token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and traces. We can provision access for your allies.
[04:52] Sana Ahmed: Audit logs—are they immutable? How long retained?
[04:55] Alex Chen: Audit logs are tamper-evident and retention is configurable; for enterprise we can set longer retention or integrate with your SIEM.
[05:03] Tom Alvarez: Any competitors we should be aware of when choosing model variants? We're also looking at Anthropic and a managed cloud provider.
[05:10] Alex Chen: Understood — we'll include a short competitive snapshot.
[05:14] [05:14] Marta Ruiz: Practical question—how do we do model rollbacks if a new model causes quality regressions?
[05:19] Priya Nair: We support pinned model versions and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback policies. Also tie quality monitoring to prompt sets so you get regression alerts.
[05:30] Devon Price: Do you support local eval harnesses so we can run tests inside our environment?
[05:34] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can provide the eval harness and runner as a docker image or script you can run in your CI.
[05:40] [05:40] Tom Alvarez: Ok great. Let's capture action items.
[05:45] Alex Chen: I'll read them out. First, Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, encryption, KMS guide) and SSO checklist.
[05:53] Jordan Lee: We'll also send the pilot runbook and benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:57] Priya Nair: I'll propose initial perf configs and the model suggestions for your 512 token workload.
[06:03] Marta Ruiz: We'll send sample prompt sets and provide test IdP details by next Monday.
[06:08] Sana Ahmed: We'll review the security pack and give feedback; expecting a follow-up call for scoping if needed.
[06:15] Alex Chen: Sounds good. Anything else before we close?
[06:18] Tom Alvarez: No, thanks. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[06:21] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone we'll email the pack and schedule next touch — milestone call for integration check at start of week 1.
[06:28] [06:28] End of recording. Note: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words; please refer to attached docs for precise specs.
